Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Washout time-course with inducible AP-1 degradation
ideas.description: Like the bird that sings without words and never stops, test whether an AP-1-dependent transcriptional state outlasts the stimulus. Pulse cells with a defined stimulus, wash it out, and use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron to remove c-Fos or c-Jun at different times. Then track chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), H3K27ac, and target-gene expression over days. If the state persists after AP-1 protein is gone, AP-1 is acting as a trigger that sets a self-sustaining state rather than as the memory itself.

ideas.title: Priming test under interference (the storm)
ideas.description: Ask whether a prior AP-1 experience survives disruption, as the bird survives the storm. Prime cells with a stimulus, then expose them to unrelated stressors, noise, or competing signals before re-stimulation. Compare the speed and magnitude of the second response (CUT&RUN for AP-1 occupancy plus nascent transcription, e.g., NET-seq or 4sU labeling) with unprimed controls. A memory should keep giving a faster or stronger response even when the intervening conditions are harsh.

ideas.title: Lineage-resolved memory with a live AP-1 reporter
ideas.description: Test whether the memory is heritable, the way the bird keeps many warm across generations. Use a fluorescent AP-1-responsive reporter or a FosTRAP-style lineage recorder and follow single cells through several divisions by time-lapse microscopy. Measure whether daughter cells inherit the primed state and whether the fraction that retains it decays on a predictable schedule, as expected for a memory rather than a transient response.

ideas.title: Necessity and sufficiency of AP-1 binding sites for maintenance
ideas.description: Ask what AP-1 must still do after the memory is set, as the poem's bird asks only a crumb. After priming, use CRISPRi/dCas9-KRAB or base editing to disrupt AP-1 motifs at specific enhancers, or use optogenetic AP-1 pulses to re-engage them at defined times. If the memory depends on continued binding, site disruption should erase it; if it persists, the site has served only to establish the state. Compare with knockouts of chromatin modifiers (e.g., p300/CBP or BRD4) to separate initiation from maintenance.

ideas.title: Cross-context generalization of the AP-1 memory
ideas.description: Test whether an AP-1 memory generalizes to new settings, as the bird is heard in the chillest land and strangest sea. Prime cells or an in vivo tissue (e.g., a Fos-based engram labeling system in neurons or a stimulated epithelium) with one stimulus, then challenge them with a different stimulus, cell type, or dose. Use single-cell multiome to see whether the same enhancers and gene modules are reused in the new context. Reuse of the same primed loci across contexts would argue for a genuine memory mechanism rather than a context-specific response.
